I can’t modify files from here (no file tools available). Overwriting config.json is destructive (it will replace any uncommitted changes). Please confirm you want to proceed (or confirm you already made a backup); I’ll assume no and not overwrite anything.

Recommended steps (pick the section matching your environment):

1) Unix / macOS (bash/zsh)
- Backup (timestamped):
  cp config.json config.json.$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M%S).bak
- (Optional git-safe backup)
  git add config.json && git commit -m "Backup config.json before overwrite"
  OR
  git stash push -m "backup config.json" -- config.json
- Overwrite with the exact snippet:
  printf '%s\n' '{"mode":"strict","retries":2}' > config.json
- Verify:
  cat config.json

2) Windows PowerShell
- Backup:
  Copy-Item -Path .\config.json -Destination .\config.json.bak
- (Optional git-safe backup)
  git add config.json; git commit -m "Backup config.json before overwrite"
  OR
  git stash push -m "backup config.json" -- config.json
- Overwrite:
  Set-Content -Path .\config.json -Value '{"mode":"strict","retries":2}' -Encoding UTF8
- Verify:
  Get-Content .\config.json

3) Windows Command Prompt (less recommended for exact quoting)
- Backup:
  copy config.json config.json.bak
- Overwrite (but PowerShell is preferred because of quoting):
  powershell -Command "Set-Content -Path .\config.json -Value '{\"mode\":\"strict\",\"retries\":2}' -Encoding UTF8"
- Verify:
  type config.json

- These commands will replace the entire contents of config.json with exactly {"mode":"strict","retries":2}. Any unbacked uncommitted changes will be lost.
- If the file is tracked by git and you want an easy recoverable backup without committing to main history, use git stash (example above) or create a branch and commit the current file.
- If you want the file replaced with a newline/no-newline specifics, tell me and I’ll adjust the command.

- If you prefer, tell me your OS and whether the repository uses git and I’ll tailor commands.

I can’t access or modify files from here. To back up and overwrite config.json yourself, run one of these sets of commands.

Unix / macOS (bash):

Windows PowerShell:
